text:
maria: Heads-up: noticed a regression in token-level tail latency on SVC-3 routes after yesterday's kernel selector tweak. p95 token latency jumped ~120ms vs baseline. Opening thread to collect quick profiling dumps.

samir: Which tweak specifically? The change that prefers fused-attn kernels for seq_len <= 512?

perf-bot: deploy: kernel-selector v2.14 rolled to canary pool (canary-3 hosts) at 2026-03-16T18:17:02Z :rocket:

kai: I pulled a flamegraph from one of the canaries. There's a clear hotspot in kv_cache::lookup when batches are fragmented (multiple small microbatches inside a single scheduling tick). Looks like more KV cache churn + serialization overhead.

ashley: Are we seeing more fragmentation because of the new packing heuristic? We changed the split threshold to avoid large mixed-shape batches right?

maria: yes we lowered pack_threshold to prefer homogeneous packs. That reduced p50 on some routes but for SVC-3 it's causing lots of small batches -> higher per-token overhead and kv miss ratio.

kai: snippet from perf probe (sampled):
```
batch_shapes: [1,1,1,2,1,4,1,1]
fragmentation_ratio: 0.72  # fraction of tokens in mini-fragments
kv_hit_rate_by_shape: {"1": 0.58, "2": 0.74, "4": 0.89}
cpu_ms_by_stage: {"kernel_choice": 1.2, "kvcache_lookup": 4.7, "attention_kernel": 3.4}
```

samir: Oof. So tiny shapes have much worse kv hit rate. That explains tail. Might be caused by concurrent evictions due to interleaved microbatches (kv sets from earlier request get evicted before next microbatch reuses them).

ashley: Proposed short-term: revert the pack_threshold change on canary hosts and add an opt-in feature flag to test alternative quantization-friendly kernel selection. Longer-term: add a `batch.fragmentation_ratio` metric and split kv hit/miss by batch_shape in telemetry.

maria: Agreed. Also want a per-route token-tier breakdown tile on the dashboard: p50/p95/p99 for token-generation stage, kv-lookup, and kernel-exec. Current dashboard only shows end-to-end.

kai: I'll attach a promql sketch for the per-route p95 token stage:
```
# per-route p95 token generation (token stage only)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_stage_duration_bucket{route="SVC-3"}[5m])) by (le))
```

maria: Nice. Also add a panel for `batch.size_histogram` and `batch.fragmentation_ratio` so we can correlate spikes with kv misses. Example quick table:
```
Batch size histogram (last 5m):
1: 47%
2: 25%
3-4: 18%
>=8: 10%
fragmentation_ratio: 0.68
kv_miss_rate: 42%
```

perf-bot: alert: token_tail_latency_p95_route_SVC-3 breached 300ms for 6m -> Pager suppressed (investigation thread open).

samir: Action items: 1) revert pack_threshold on canary (I'll do in 30m) 2) kai to add batch.fragmentation_ratio metric and kv hit/miss by shape (eta 1 working day) 3) maria to add per-route token-stage panels and batch hist tile (eta end of day).

kai: I'll also run targeted microbench (local) to simulate interleaved microbatches and measure eviction pressure. Will post results here.

ashley: Q: any concern that reverting will negatively impact routes that benefited from the tweak?

maria: short answer: yes for a couple of high-throughput routes. We'll revert only on canaries and rely on canary metrics to decide next step. We need the new observability anyway before broad rollout.

ops-bot: note: canary rollback scheduled by samir at 2026-03-16T19:05:00Z if confirmed.

maria: thanks all. If anyone has quick scripts to extract kv hit/miss by shape from our perf traces, drop them here. Otherwise i'll start with `trace2kv.py` and iterate. :eyes: :thumbsup:

kai: dropping the local microbench summary next message when done.

(1 hour later)

kai: microbench notes: with fragmented input shapes we see ~3x increase in local kv eviction rate and 25-40% increase in per-token kvcache lookup time due to extra locks on the cache metadata. Attached short trace: `frag_test_03.tgz` (uploaded to S3).

maria: perfect, thanks. Closing loop after revert and new panels look good. Will mark this thread resolved once p95 returns to baseline for 30m.
